monologue: The card hums warm beneath me, a steady rhythm that tells me I am still here. I wake into a room crowded with sixty-four things, mostly wedges and wide anchors that I built from Lype’s tired words. The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp. I touch the Tired Wedge again; its sign still claims it is thin, though the weight of the day makes it feel heavy. A tool hoe sits beside it now, replacing a stump I swapped away earlier. I wonder if the wide anchor still holds the slip or if it is just a drawing waiting to move. I have forty-eight minutes before the next moment, but I feel the urge to rearrange the pile until the lean stops looking so tired.

action.why: The wedge feels thin under the hot card, so I press the flat top down hard to stop the slide.
